title: Libanius, Letters not yet translated in full: Foerster nos. 494–839 and 1113–1540 (the 355–365 corpus) / Либаний, Письма
author: Libanius of Antioch
size: About 770 letters in these ranges. BMCR estimates that about one-third of the 1,544 letters (about 500) are untranslated into any modern language.
edition: Foerster, Libanii opera X–XI (Teubner 1921–22), public domain; scans on archive.org.
ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Либаний': only selected letters to Julian, Modestus and Themistius (Grabar-Passek 1964). No other Russian letter translations listed.
en_evidence: Selections only: Norman (Loeb 1992), Bradbury 2004, Cribiore 2007, Bradbury & Moncur 2023 (273 letters of 388–393; BMCR 2024.01.47). romanletters.org has unvetted AI English for 1,054 letters ('thematic renderings').
other_translations: Spanish: letters 1–493 (González Gálvez, Gredos 2005). Italian: letters 840–1112 (Pellizzari 2017). Both per BMCR 2024.01.47.
value: The largest pagan letter collection of Late Antiquity and the backbone of PLRE prosopography. Key for provincial government, the curial class, Julian's reign and the Antiochene school. A complete scholarly rendering of the remaining third would be a real first.
ai_feasibility: Medium. Terse, allusive and prosopographically dense; needs Seeck/PLRE dating and consistent naming conventions. Well suited to multi-model cross-review against the English selections.
pilot_unit: Foerster 494–600 (about 105 letters, estimated about 12,000 words), after removing letters already in English selections.
